clue.text: Tree put in between river and edge of road

indicators.note: the word in is placed between the river and the road's edge, as a filling

parts.note: the Tamar is a river forming the Devon-Cornwall border

indicators.note: the edge of a word here is its final letter, the end of road

explanation.surface: Someone planting a tree on the verge between a river and a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' places the word 'in' between the river and the road's last letter. The Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical leguminous species grown for its sour pods.

clue.text: Activist old volunteers to put in raised capital

indicators.note: the volunteers and the word to are placed inside the capital city
in a down clue, raised means the city's name is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve of volunteer soldiers, now renamed

explanation.surface: A campaigner's veteran helpers are being installed in the upper part of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the capital upwards, as a down clue reads; 'put in' lodges the other pieces inside. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up public feeling for a cause, as a campaigner does.

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the word for profundity loses its final letter, its end

parts.note: depth is profundity

explanation.surface: A grammar note praising a writer's skill and their unending profundity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the final letter off the synonym for profundity.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly skilled, so a masterly performance is an adept one.

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Scholars have drawn up a list of the top people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the fourteen letters of AN ELITE LISTING.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia is the intellectual class, the scholars and thinkers of a society.

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
taken as written
something posted has been sent by mail

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician's objection is put in the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement or objection voiced against authority.

indicators.note: the instrument's letters are used within the run of the next words

explanation.surface: A musical instrument appears in a short improvised piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join: impromp-TU BA-gatelle.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is a large low-pitched brass wind instrument.

clue.text: Highly confidential operations wrapped up by investigator on time

indicators.note: the operations are enclosed inside the investigator's short title

parts.note: tec is short for detective
ops is the short form of operations
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A detective keeps covert operations under wraps and finishes on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped up by' sets the operations inside the detective's short title; 'on' is read as 'regarding', not as a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Top secret is the highest classification of restricted government information.

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so the word for nonsense holds the others

parts.note: bosh is nonsense
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Childish silliness amusing the first-year pupils at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts Y and I inside BOSH; 'Year One' is the first class of English primary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish means youthful or like a young lad, hence juvenile.

clue.text: Original song in Great Britain about a monarch

indicators.note: the song sits inside the abbreviation for Great Britain

parts.note: a round is a song sung in overlapping parts
re means about
taken as written
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A national anthem about a sovereign, sung across Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the song inside the abbreviation for Great Britain; 'about' is read as 'regarding'. A round is a song for staggered voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundbreaking work is innovative, breaking new ground, and so original.

clue.text: Dreadful act not having a point

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: the word act goes without the letter given by a

explanation.surface: A terrible deed that serves no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having a' removes that letter from 'act'. 'point' here is a verb, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to aim or guide them, as you point a way.

indicators.note: the agent swallows the drink, so the drink goes inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: turned means the drink's letters are read backwards

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A secret agent who had been drinking became quarrelsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the drink and 'consuming' puts it inside the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and quick to quarrel.

clue.text: Sweet marzipan, for instance, badly wrapped

indicators.note: the word for badly is wrapped inside the paste

parts.note: marzipan is an almond paste, an example of a paste
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A confection of marzipan that has been poorly packaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped' puts the synonym for badly inside the paste; marzipan is almond paste.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewy confection or lozenge.

clue.text: Nervous as union leader, when gripped by revolutionary urge

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the word as is held inside the reversed urge
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or urge

explanation.surface: A trade union boss is anxious when seized by radical impulses.
explanation.walkthrough: U from 'union' comes first; 'revolutionary' turns YEN into NEY, which grips AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasy means troubled and anxious, without calm.

clue.text: Subjugator in dour action's wrongly imprisoning queen

indicators.note: the jumbled letters lock up the abbreviation for queen
wrongly means the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: A conqueror's grim deeds included jailing a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges the eleven letters, the 's counting as one, and 'imprisoning' sets the queen's letter among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquistador was a Spanish conqueror of the Americas, one who subjugated peoples.

parts.note: qua means as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: drilled means trained or instructed

explanation.surface: Dancers performing exactly as they were taught, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from the synonym for instructed; qua is Latin-derived English for 'in the capacity of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quadrille is a square dance for four couples, popular in the 1800s.

indicators.note: the word for drop goes inside the payment

parts.note: the dole is state unemployment payment in Britain
to omit is to drop or leave out

explanation.surface: A cut in someone's wages to pay for stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' is a verb, not the fall in payment the surface paints. The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolomite is a sedimentary mineral of calcium magnesium carbonate.

indicators.note: new means the letters are freshly made into another arrangement

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech or address

explanation.surface: A fresh e-mail address works better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges EMAIL into AMELI, followed by ORATION; 'address' is a speech, not a mail address.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelioration is the act of making something better.

definitions.meaning: a fragrant smoke from burning spices or gum
as a verb, to enrage or infuriate

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a perfume from burnt resin; the verb, stressed on the second syllable, means to make furious.

parts.note: ham is meat from a pig's leg
per means for each

explanation.surface: Picnic food: meat packed for everyone in a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a wicker basket for picnic food or gifts.

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone echoes the usual nonsense without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words without understanding, as the talking bird does.

definitions.meaning: as an informal adjective, first-rate or splendid
as a verb, to fight for or back a cause

explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang uses it for splendid; as a verb it means to advocate a cause.

clue.text: Fighter, for example, said to be unmarked

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, giving its homophone

parts.note: a fighter is a military plane

explanation.surface: A military jet is reported to carry no insignia.
explanation.walkthrough: A fighter is an aircraft, not a boxer, which the surface tempts.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means without decoration or markings.

indicators.note: round means the word is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat walks round the rim of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses the edge, not a cat circling something as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillion is the passenger seat behind a motorcycle rider.

clue.text: Sloping island, one covered with powder

indicators.note: the powder surrounds and covers the number one

parts.note: talc is a soft powder
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A tilted island, one part blanketed in dust.
explanation.walkthrough: I (island), then I (one) placed inside TALC.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slants to the right.

indicators.note: the king's letter sits inside the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A broad-minded monarch is running the show.
explanation.walkthrough: R (rex) goes inside FEE; 'in charge' is not a unit but two words with separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Free can mean generous or unrestrained, as a liberal hand gives freely.

clue.text: Objective in development of green cause

indicators.note: the objective is placed inside the rearranged letters
development means the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: The goal of developing green policies is a worthy cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges the colour's letters and 'in' places the objective among them; 'cause' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to bring about or give rise to something.
